## Why

The graph design UI routes for approving and rejecting AI-generated proposals do not catch invalid proposal state transitions (`src/lms/ui/graph_design.py:96-150`). In `approve_graph_proposal_route` and `reject_graph_proposal_route`, calls to `approve_proposal` and `reject_proposal` execute without handling `InvalidProposalStateError` or `ProposalNotFoundError`. When an author double-clicks the action button or processes an already-resolved proposal across multiple browser tabs, the server raises an unhandled exception resulting in HTTP 500 error pages. The UI should catch already-resolved proposal exceptions, flash a user notice, and redirect back to `/app/admin/graph-design` with HTTP 303. This is a verified **current break** in UI error handling.

## Scope

Wrap proposal approval and rejection service calls in `src/lms/ui/graph_design.py` in try-except blocks catching `(InvalidProposalStateError, ProposalNotFoundError)`, add feedback flash notices, and return HTTP 303 redirect responses. Add regression tests in `tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT modify the authoring assist service in `src/lms/llm/authoring_assist.py`.
- Do NOT modify the proposal data model in `src/lms/llm/proposals.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding try-except blocks without redirecting to `/app/admin/graph-design` with flash error messages or without test coverage of already-resolved proposals is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/lms/ui/graph_design.py`, import `InvalidProposalStateError` and `ProposalNotFoundError` from `src/lms/llm/proposals.py`.
- [ ] In `src/lms/ui/graph_design.py`, update `approve_graph_proposal_route` and `reject_graph_proposal_route` to catch `(InvalidProposalStateError, ProposalNotFoundError)` and return a redirect response to `/app/admin/graph-design` with a flash warning message.
- [ ] In `tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py`, add test `test_graph_design_duplicate_proposal_approval_redirects_with_notice` asserting that approving an already-approved proposal returns HTTP 303 redirect with a notice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The named test `pytest tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py -k "test_graph_design_duplicate_proposal_approval_redirects_with_notice"` passes with 0 failures, asserting HTTP 303 redirect when approving or rejecting an already-resolved proposal.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** In `src/lms/ui/graph_design.py:105`, comment out the exception handler for `InvalidProposalStateError`. Running `pytest tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py -k "test_graph_design_duplicate_proposal_approval_redirects_with_notice"` MUST fail (unhandled exception raised instead of HTTP 303 redirect). Revert the edit after capturing the failure.
- [ ] Existing graph design surface tests pass via `pytest tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Use `request.session.flash("Proposal has already been processed", "warning")` pattern consistent with support admin UI routes in `src/lms/ui/support_admin.py`.
- Confirmed-green test runner: `pytest tests/ui/test_graph_design_surface.py`
title: Handle duplicate proposal state transitions gracefully in graph design UI routes

## Why

The float parsing helper in the capability repository lacks non-numeric string and `NaN` validation (`src/lms/capability/repository.py:221-240`). In `_as_float(value)`, the function performs `if isinstance(value, int | float | str): return float(value)`. Unlike `_as_int`, it lacks try-except protection against invalid strings such as empty strings. In addition, when `value` is `float("nan")` or `"nan"`, `_as_float` returns `nan`. When checking capability target thresholds (`_as_float(row["current_estimate"]) < target.confidence_threshold`), comparisons against `NaN` evaluate to `False`, silently masking weak nodes from learner gap analyses. This is a verified **latent fragility** and calculation robustness issue.

## Scope

Update `_as_float` in `src/lms/capability/repository.py` to safely catch conversion exceptions and validate `math.isfinite(parsed_val)`, returning a safe fallback default or raising a validation error. Add regression tests in `tests/capability/test_repository.py`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT modify Bayesian mastery formulas in `src/lms/mastery/policy.py`.
- Do NOT alter table schema definitions in `src/lms/capability/models.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: returning 0.0 for all string inputs without checking finite bounds or without adding unit test assertions for NaN and malformed string handling is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/lms/capability/repository.py`, import `math` and update `_as_float` to catch `(ValueError, TypeError)` and verify `math.isfinite(parsed_val)`, returning `default` when value is non-numeric, `NaN`, or infinite.
- [ ] In `src/lms/capability/repository.py`, ensure aggregate estimation queries handle null or non-finite mastery records safely without returning `NaN` scores.
- [ ] In `tests/capability/test_repository.py`, add test `test_as_float_handles_nan_and_invalid_strings_safely` asserting safe fallback behavior for `NaN`, `Inf`, and invalid string inputs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The named test `pytest tests/capability/test_repository.py -k "test_as_float_handles_nan_and_invalid_strings_safely"` passes with 0 failures, asserting that `_as_float` returns the fallback value for `float("nan")`, `"nan"`, `float("inf")`, and non-numeric strings.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** In `src/lms/capability/repository.py:225`, remove the `math.isfinite` check in `_as_float`. Running `pytest tests/capability/test_repository.py -k "test_as_float_handles_nan_and_invalid_strings_safely"` MUST fail with an assertion failure (expecting fallback value but receiving `nan`). Revert the edit after capturing the failure.
- [ ] Existing capability repository tests pass via `pytest tests/capability/test_repository.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Align `_as_float` error handling with `_as_int` in `src/lms/capability/repository.py:230-245`.
- Confirmed-green test runner: `pytest tests/capability/test_repository.py`
title: Add non-numeric string and NaN validation to capability repository float parsing

## Why

Criterion points validation in rubric scoring accepts `NaN` (not-a-number) floating-point values without rejection (`src/lms/feedback/scoring.py:233-237`). In `_normalize_criterion_scores`, points are parsed via `points = float(item.get("points", 0))` and validated with `if points < 0 or points > criterion.max_points:`. In Python, comparisons against `float("nan")` always evaluate to `False`, allowing `NaN` values to bypass boundary checks. This causes `raw_score = nan` and `normalized_score = nan` to propagate into `EvidenceRecord` and downstream database models. When persisted, SQLite rejects `NaN` in `NOT NULL` columns or stores corrupt non-numeric values, triggering unhandled `sqlite3.IntegrityError` (HTTP 500) rather than raising `InvalidRubricScoringError` (HTTP 422). This is a verified **current break** in rubric scoring boundary validation.

## Scope

Add explicit `math.isfinite(points)` checks in `_normalize_criterion_scores` in `src/lms/feedback/scoring.py`. Raise `InvalidRubricScoringError` when criterion points contain `NaN`, `Inf`, or `-Inf`. Add unit test coverage in `tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT alter valid integer and floating-point scoring computations in `score_rubric`.
- Do NOT alter template models in `src/lms/feedback/templates.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding `math.isnan` without checking `math.isinf` or without raising `InvalidRubricScoringError` on invalid scores is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/lms/feedback/scoring.py`, import `math` and add a finite numeric check `if not math.isfinite(points): raise InvalidRubricScoringError(f"Points for criterion {criterion.id} must be a finite number")` inside `_normalize_criterion_scores`.
- [ ] In `src/lms/feedback/scoring.py`, ensure parsing errors from non-numeric string values raise `InvalidRubricScoringError` cleanly.
- [ ] In `tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py`, add test `test_score_rubric_rejects_nan_and_inf_points` asserting that `score_rubric` raises `InvalidRubricScoringError` when criterion points contain `float("nan")` or `float("inf")`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The named test `pytest tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py -k "test_score_rubric_rejects_nan_and_inf_points"` passes with 0 failures, asserting `InvalidRubricScoringError` is raised when scoring input contains `float("nan")` or `float("inf")`.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** In `src/lms/feedback/scoring.py`, comment out the `math.isfinite(points)` check in `_normalize_criterion_scores`. Running `pytest tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py -k "test_score_rubric_rejects_nan_and_inf_points"` MUST fail with `Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'lms.feedback.scoring.InvalidRubricScoringError'>`. Revert the edit after capturing the failure.
- [ ] Existing rubric scoring tests pass via `pytest tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Validate finite status before comparing against minimum and maximum points: `try: points = float(item.get("points", 0)) except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc: raise InvalidRubricScoringError(...) from exc`.
- Confirmed-green test runner: `pytest tests/feedback/test_rubric_scoring.py`
title: Validate finite numeric bounds in rubric criterion scoring to prevent NaN propagation

## Why

The LLM trace-control API endpoint accepts arbitrary client-specified `actor_id` values and does not enforce authentication or learner ownership authorization (`src/lms/llm/api.py:657-686`). `control_llm_trace_route` (`POST /llm/sessions/{session_id}/trace-control`) accepts `payload: LLMTraceControlRequest` and checks only `if llm_session.learner_id != payload.actor_id: raise HTTPException(404)`. The route omits `CurrentUserDep` and `SettingsDep` and never validates that the authenticated caller matches `payload.actor_id` or owns the session. In deployed auth mode (`settings.auth_required = True`), an authenticated learner Alice can supply `actor_id = <bob_learner_id>` and trigger `action: "forget"` on Bob's private LLM session, wiping Bob's `response_summary` and modifying trace retention states. This is a verified **current break** and authorization bypass vulnerability.

## Scope

Inject `CurrentUserDep` and `SettingsDep` into `control_llm_trace_route` in `src/lms/llm/api.py`. Call `require_learner_ownership(session, user=current_user, settings=settings, learner_id=llm_session.learner_id)` and verify that `payload.actor_id` matches the authenticated learner identity. Add regression tests in `tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT modify the trace control transition state machine in `src/lms/llm/trace_controls.py`.
- Do NOT modify session creation or prompt execution routes in `src/lms/llm/api.py`.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: modifying the route signature without calling `require_learner_ownership` or without adding test assertions verifying foreign session trace control rejection is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/lms/llm/api.py`, import `CurrentUserDep`, `SettingsDep`, and `require_learner_ownership` from `src/lms/auth/dependencies.py`.
- [ ] In `src/lms/llm/api.py`, update `control_llm_trace_route` signature to accept `current_user: CurrentUserDep` and `settings: SettingsDep`, and call `require_learner_ownership(session, user=current_user, settings=settings, learner_id=llm_session.learner_id)`.
- [ ] In `src/lms/llm/api.py`, verify that `payload.actor_id` matches the authenticated `current_user.learner_id` when authentication is enabled.
- [ ] In `tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py`, add test `test_control_llm_trace_foreign_learner_rejected` verifying that attempting trace control on another learner's session returns HTTP 404 when authentication is enabled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The named test `pytest tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py -k "test_control_llm_trace_foreign_learner_rejected"` passes with 0 failures, asserting HTTP 404 when an authenticated user attempts trace control on a foreign LLM session.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** In `src/lms/llm/api.py:666`, remove the `require_learner_ownership` call in `control_llm_trace_route`. Running `pytest tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py -k "test_control_llm_trace_foreign_learner_rejected"` MUST fail (receiving HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 404). Revert the edit after capturing the failure.
- [ ] Existing deployed learner ownership tests pass via `pytest tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py`.

## Implementation Notes

- Follow the ownership enforcement pattern established across `tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py:50-120`.
- Confirmed-green test runner: `pytest tests/api/test_deployed_learner_ownership.py`

## Why

In `src/lms/ui/support_admin.py:44-71, 116-160`, `support_dashboard_route` (`GET /app/support`) renders `_support_signals(session)`, which iterates over open `FeedbackAction` and `EvidenceRecord` rows across all learners in the database. ## Why
This repo's aggregate line coverage is 90.06% (10,805 statements), already at or above the fleet's 90% target. **This issue is explicitly NOT about raising that percentage further.** An aggregate number can hide a completely untested critical module sitting behind many well-tested small ones — 90% overall is fully consistent with one important, complex feature being almost entirely untested. The goal is to find real risk: a feature or function whose failure would actually matter, that currently has thin or no test coverage, where a small number of well-chosen tests would meaningfully reduce the chance of a future regression going unnoticed.

## Method
1. Enumerate this repo's major features / business-critical code paths by reading its own README, entry points, and architecture docs — do not guess from the repo name or from this issue.
2. For each major feature, check ITS OWN coverage specifically (not the repo aggregate) — which files/functions implement it, and what fraction of them is actually exercised. A repo at 90.06% overall can easily have one 200-line module sitting at 20%.
3. Rank candidates by (a) how central the feature is to the app's actual purpose, (b) how complex or edge-case-prone the code is (branching logic, external I/O, state machines, data-integrity or financial calculations), and (c) how thin its real coverage is — not by raw statement count and not by how easy a test would be to write.
4. Before writing anything, confirm the top candidate is a REAL risk: read the code, articulate a concrete plausible failure (a bad input, a boundary condition, a state transition, a silent wrong answer) — not a hypothetical one. If nothing clears that bar, say so; do not manufacture a gap to fill.
5. Write ONE FOCUSED test (or a small tightly related few) pinning correct behavior for that specific risk, with the same discipline as every other round in this initiative: it must FAIL when the code is deliberately broken and PASS when reverted. Prove this for real — run the break and the revert, don't assert it.
6. If you find an ACTUAL BUG while investigating (not just a coverage gap), fix it with a minimal, targeted diff in the same PR.

## Report (required, in the PR body or a comment if no action is warranted)
Name the features you considered, which one you picked and why, the concrete failure mode the new test guards against, and what it actually proves. If no gap you found is worth closing, say so explicitly and explain why the major features are already adequately covered where it matters — that is a valid, useful outcome and is preferred over padding the number.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Named test: the new test(s), proving the identified risk is now caught.
- Deliberate-break -> revert: break the specific behavior the test targets, confirm the named test FAILS, revert, confirm it passes again. Report the transcript.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT chase the coverage percentage — a test that pads the number without addressing a genuine breakage risk does not satisfy this issue.
- Do NOT refactor working code or touch unrelated files.
- Low blast radius only; one PR for the one risk you identify as highest-value.

_Part of the fleet coverage-calibration initiative. The goal is to improve the code, not a metric._

## Why (verified evidence)

`stranske/learning-management-system` tracks a root `node_modules/` tree that nothing depends on, inflating every clone, CI checkout and agent worktree of the repo.

- **`node_modules/` at the repo root is tracked: 356 files, 7,353,094 bytes** — 50.2% of the repo's 14,633,789 tracked bytes. Verified via `GET /repos/stranske/learning-management-system/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1`.
- **There is no `package.json` anywhere at the repo root**, so the tree cannot even be reinstalled reproducibly from it. It is residue from `npm install --no-save`, which by definition writes no manifest.
- **Nothing consumes it.** `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml:521` runs `npm install --no-save --no-package-lock @octokit/rest @octokit/auth-app` at job time, so CI installs `@octokit` fresh rather than reading the committed copy. The tracked tree's top-level packages are exactly the `@octokit` dependency closure (`@octokit`, `before-after-hook`, `fast-content-type-parse`, `toad-cache`, `universal-github-app-jwt`, `universal-user-agent`).
- **`.gitignore:16`** is the end of the file and contains no `node_modules` pattern, so nothing prevents the tree growing back.
- `tests/__pycache__` is tracked (15,088B) even though `__pycache__/` is already in `.gitignore` — an ignore rule does not untrack what is already committed.

### The one thing that must not break

`.github/scripts/node_modules/` (84 files) is **deliberately vendored** and must stay tracked:

- `.github/scripts/package.json` declares `"minimatch": "file:node_modules/minimatch"` — a self-referential `file:` dependency on the committed tree.
- `.github/workflows/agents-auto-pilot.yml:207-208` copies `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/node_modules` into `workflows-lib/`.
- `.github/workflows/agents-guard.yml:81-82,151-152` allowlists `.github/scripts/node_modules/minimatch` as a protected path.

A bare `node_modules/` ignore pattern matches at **every depth** and would swallow this tree, breaking auto-pilot and the guard. The pattern added below is root-anchored (`/node_modules/`).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `/node_modules/` (root-anchored, leading slash **required**) to `.gitignore` after line 16, with a comment naming why it is anchored.
- [ ] `git rm -r --cached node_modules` — untracks 356 files / 7,353,094 bytes from HEAD.
- [ ] `git rm -r --cached tests/__pycache__` — 15,088B, already matched by `.gitignore:13` (`__pycache__/`) yet still tracked.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_repo_hygiene.py` with the named test below.

## Test gate

- **Named test:** `tests/test_repo_hygiene.py::test_generated_dirs_untracked_and_vendored_preserved`, asserting all four:
  1. `git ls-files node_modules` returns **no** paths (root tree untracked).
  2. `git ls-files .github/scripts/node_modules` returns **at least one** path (vendored tree still tracked).
  3. `git check-ignore -q node_modules/probe.js` **succeeds** (root tree is ignored going forward).
  4. `git check-ignore -q .github/scripts/node_modules/minimatch/package.json` **fails** (vendored tree is NOT ignored).
- **Deliberate-break → revert:** change the `.gitignore` entry from `/node_modules/` to a bare `node_modules/`, run the named test, confirm **assertion 4 FAILS** (the vendored tree becomes ignored), then revert to `/node_modules/` and confirm the test passes again.

## Non-Goals

- Do **NOT** untrack, ignore, move or modify `.github/scripts/node_modules/` or `.github/scripts/package.json` — see the evidence above; both are load-bearing.
- Do **NOT** rewrite git history. `git rm -r --cached` shrinks HEAD, clones and archives; shrinking history needs `git-filter-repo` and a force-push that rebases every open PR, and is deliberately out of scope.
- Do **NOT** add a bare `node_modules/` pattern anywhere, including a global or nested `.gitignore`.
- Do **NOT** propagate the full `BEGIN/END WORKFLOWS STATUS FILES` managed block — this repo's `.gitignore` does not currently carry it, and adding it is a separate change.
- Do **NOT** change any workflow file.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task is a concrete edit verified by the gate above.

_Surfaced by the Orchestrator consumer-sync ingest's repo-hygiene report (2026-08-20), which reads each consumer repo through the git tree API. Verified against `GET /repos/stranske/learning-management-system/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1` and the cited workflow lines. Prevention for newly-created repos is stranske/Workflows#3145, which adds the same root-anchored pattern to the consumer template; this issue removes what is already tracked here._

## Why (verified evidence)

The documented local run path — `docker compose up` (README / `docker-compose.yml`) — **does not start the app**. Two independent bugs block it; both reproduced on a clean checkout, 2026-06-22:

**1. Postgres 18 data-directory layout (db container exits)**
- `docker-compose.yml` mounts `lms_pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` (legacy path), but `image: postgres:18-alpine` changed its layout to major-version subdirs under `/var/lib/postgresql`.
- The db container errors and exits: *"Counter to that, there appears to be PostgreSQL data in: /var/lib/postgresql/data (unused mount/volume)"* (see docker-library/postgres#1259). The `app` service then fails with "dependency failed to start".
- Fix: mount the volume at `/var/lib/postgresql` (not `/var/lib/postgresql/data`).

**2. Editable install path invalid in the runtime image (`No module named 'lms'`)**
- `Dockerfile` builder runs `pip install --no-deps -e .` from `/build`, so the editable record points at `/build/src`. The runtime stage then `COPY --from=builder /build /app` (sources at **`/app/src`**) — but the editable `.pth`/record still references the nonexistent **`/build/src`**.
- Result: the app container crashes at startup — `alembic upgrade head` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lms'`. (Render uses the native `render.yaml` runtime, so this only bites the Docker/local-compose path.)
- Fix: make `lms` importable in the runtime image — e.g. set `WORKDIR`/`PYTHONPATH` so `/app/src` is on the path, or perform the editable install in the runtime stage against `/app`, or build a real wheel.

**User-facing consequence:** a new contributor (or the owner on a fresh machine) cannot run the LMS locally via the documented command without patching two files. With both patched locally, the app starts cleanly (`Uvicorn running… Application startup complete`) and the UI renders.

## Tasks
- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` (db service) — change the volume mount from `lms_pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` to `lms_pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql` for `postgres:18-alpine`.
- [ ] `Dockerfile` — ensure `lms` is importable in the runtime stage (add `ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/src`, or re-run the editable install / install a wheel in the runtime image), so `alembic` + `uvicorn lms.main:app` start without `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- [ ] (minor) Root `/` returns `{"detail":"Not Found"}` (JSON 404) — add a redirect to the UI entry (or a minimal landing) so the base URL isn't a bare 404.

## Test gate
- Named test/CI check: a compose smoke test (e.g. `tests/test_compose_smoke` or a CI job) that runs `docker compose up -d`, waits for the `app` healthcheck (`/health`) to pass, and asserts `GET /app/admin` returns 200 — i.e. the stack starts end-to-end from a clean volume.
- Deliberate-break → revert: restore `:/var/lib/postgresql/data` (or remove the PYTHONPATH/install fix) → confirm the smoke test FAILS (db exits / `No module named lms`) → revert.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT change the Render `render.yaml` native-runtime path (it works); fix the Docker/compose local-dev path.
- Do NOT change app logic; this is build/run configuration only.

_Surfaced by the UX Review (`Code/Orchestrator/ux_review.py`) first pass, 2026-06-22 — Gate-1/runnability blocker (the app couldn't be started via the documented path). Verified by reproducing both failures on a clean checkout and confirming the app starts after both fixes._

## Why

The app-behavior baseline kit (PR #229) caught a real cross-environment robustness issue in the spaced-repetition scheduler. For a "supported success" attempt (correct answer, high confidence, `support_level: hint`), the emitted FSRS rating (`evidence_to_fsrs_rating`) is **3 ("good") on macOS but 2 ("hard") on Linux CI** — for identical inputs. This is non-determinism across environments in a user-facing scheduling decision.

## Scope

Root cause (traced via `tests/baseline/adapter.py` → `schedule_from_attempt` → `evidence_to_fsrs_rating`):

- `fsrs_adapter._score()` returns `record.normalized_score` **verbatim** (no blend).
- The score-threshold rules (`partial-under-half`, `partial-under-mastery`, `partial-at-mastery`) each require a **non-None** score. The categorical `supported-or-low-confidence-correct` rule (triggered by `support_level: hint`) yields rating 2.
- On macOS the scenario's `normalized_score` (e.g. 0.97) is present at FSRS time → `partial-at-mastery` fires → rating **3**. On Linux CI `normalized_score` arrives as **None** at FSRS time → all score rules are skipped → fall through to the support rule → rating **2**.

So a high score *silently overrides* the support signal when present, and whether the score survives to FSRS time differs by environment — making the rating environment-dependent. (The baseline test was stabilized in PR #229 by setting the scenario's score to `null` so both environments deterministically rate 2; this issue tracks the underlying scheduler behavior.)

## Non-Goals

- Re-blessing baseline goldens (already handled in PR #229).
- Changing the FSRS day-interval ramp.

## Tasks

- [ ] Investigate why `normalized_score` can arrive as `None` at FSRS time on some environments (likely a falsy/`0.0` check or a serialization/round-trip edge in the evidence pipeline between `create_evidence_record` and `evidence_to_fsrs_rating`). Ensure a set score is never silently dropped.
- [ ] Decide and make explicit the intended rule precedence: should a *supported* (hinted) correct answer always be rated "hard" (2) regardless of score, or should a high score override the support signal? Order `FSRS_RULES` accordingly so the outcome does not depend on score-presence.
- [ ] Harden `low_confidence_success` (catalog uses `normalized_score: 0.90` → rating 3 via `partial-at-mastery`): it has the same latent fragility and would drop to 2 if its score ever vanished on Linux.
- [ ] Add a unit test pinning the rating for a supported-correct attempt across both the score-present and score-absent paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `evidence_to_fsrs_rating` produces the same rating for a given attempt regardless of platform/environment (no dependence on incidental score presence).
- [ ] Rule precedence between score-threshold rules and the support/confidence rule is explicit and documented.
- [ ] A regression test covers a supported-correct attempt with score present and with score absent.

## Implementation Notes

- Key files: `src/lms/scheduling/fsrs_adapter.py` (`_score`, `FSRS_RULES`, `_is_score_at_mastery`), `src/lms/scheduling/service.py` (`schedule_from_attempt`).
- Surfaced by the baseline kit; see `tests/baseline/` (`catalog.yaml` `supported_success`, `adapter.py`).

body:
## Why

`get_session` (`src/lms/db/session.py:36-53`) wraps `session_scope()`, which unconditionally calls `session.commit()` when the generator resumes without an exception. Verified empirically (patching `get_engine` to in-memory SQLite and counting SQLAlchemy commit events with the **real** `get_session`): a plain `GET /audit/events` triggers exactly one COMMIT. Consequences:

1. Every read endpoint opens a read/write transaction and commits it, taking write-path overhead and holding locks longer than a read-only transaction would.
2. Routes that signal failure by **returning** a non-2xx response instead of raising — e.g. `login_submit` (`src/lms/auth/login.py:141-148`) returning the 401 login form — still commit.
3. Write routes that already call `commit()` then double-commit.

**Latent** correctness/efficiency defect (no data corruption today, since writes are idempotent on commit), but the transaction ownership is wrong.

## Scope

Make `get_session` read-by-default (no auto-commit); leave explicit `commit()` to write routes. `src/lms/db/session.py` (+ confirm write routes commit explicitly). `session_scope` for scripts/services keeps commit-on-exit.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change `session_scope`'s commit-on-exit behavior for scripts/services.
- Do NOT rewrite write-route logic beyond ensuring each mutation commits explicitly.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a change where a GET still emits a COMMIT, or where a write route silently stops persisting, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Change `get_session` (`db/session.py:36-53`) to yield the session and only rollback+close in teardown (no auto-commit), leaving `commit()` to write routes.
- [ ] Audit write routes that relied on the dependency's implicit commit and add an explicit `session.commit()` where missing (grep routers for mutations lacking a commit).
- [ ] Add `tests/db/test_session.py` that counts SQLAlchemy `commit` events via an event listener: a read-only GET emits **0** commits; a write route still persists its mutation.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture the FAIL output, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/db/test_session.py::test_get_request_does_not_commit` passes: a GET through a `get_session`-backed route emits 0 COMMITs (counted via a SQLAlchemy `commit` event listener).
- [ ] A write-route test confirms the mutation is still persisted after the request (no lost write).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily restore the auto-commit in `get_session`. `test_get_request_does_not_commit` **must FAIL** (1 commit on a GET). Restore the fix; it passes. Capture both runs.
- [ ] Full suite `pytest -q` stays green (no route lost its persistence).

## Implementation Notes

- Reproduction (confirmed): patch `get_engine` to in-memory SQLite, attach a `commit` event listener, issue `GET /audit/events` with the real `get_session` → 1 COMMIT observed.
- ⚠️ Blast radius: this changes transaction ownership for every write route — verify each mutation still commits and run the full `pytest -q`.

## Why

Several verified auth-surface hardening gaps in `src/lms/auth/`. Most are **latent/low** (the deployed surface is small; some are intentional v1 deferrals, noted below), but they are cheap, localized hardening of the production login path:

1. **No password strength policy.** The only constraint is `hash_password()` rejecting empty input (`passwords.py:39-43`). The bootstrap CLI `lms auth create-user`/`set-password` (`__main__.py:584,598` via `_resolve_password` at `555-572`) accepts any non-empty string (e.g. `"a"`) for the first credentialed/admin account on a deployed `AUTH_REQUIRED=true` instance.
2. **`verify_password` 500 on malformed hash.** It catches only `VerifyMismatchError` (`passwords.py:59-62`); a non-Argon2/corrupted stored hash raises `InvalidHashError`, which bubbles out of `authenticate()`→`login_submit()` as a 500 rather than a failed login. Latent (all writes use `hash_password`) until a botched migration/manual edit.
3. **Email accepted without format validation.** `UserCreate.email` is `str | None` with only `max_length` (`schemas.py:15`) — `"not-an-email"` is accepted into the unique email column.
4. **Open-redirect guard untested.** `_safe_next_path` (`login.py:64-67`) is the only open-redirect defense on the post-login `next` param; coverage shows its rejection branches (lines 65, 67) are never hit.
5. **Deleted-user revocation untested.** The stale-session→deleted-user branch (`login.py:196-201`, lines 199-200) that clears a cookie for a deleted account is never exercised.
6. **No login rate-limiting/lockout** (`login.py:124-150`) and **no password max-length** (`login.py:129`). Note: lockout/rate-limit is an **intentional v1 deferral** per `docs/architecture/auth.md:104` — surfaced for reconsideration, not as a regression.

## Scope

Localized hardening of `src/lms/auth/{passwords,schemas,login}.py` plus focused tests for the two security guards.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT build a full rate-limiting/Redis subsystem here; rate-limit/lockout is a documented v1 deferral (`docs/architecture/auth.md:104`) — add at most a lightweight per-IP+username counter if trivial, otherwise leave the deferral intact and note it.
- Do NOT change the session-cookie design or the Argon2 cost parameters.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a `validate_password_strength` helper that `hash_password` does not actually call, or tests that do not exercise the rejection branches, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `validate_password_strength(plaintext)` to `src/lms/auth/passwords.py` (min length ~12) and call it from `hash_password()` (`passwords.py:32-43`) so every path (CLI create-user/set-password, future routes) is covered; raise `ValueError` with a clear message.
- [ ] Broaden the `except` in `verify_password` (`passwords.py:59-62`) to also catch `argon2.exceptions.InvalidHashError`/`Argon2Error` and return `False`.
- [ ] Change `UserCreate.email` (`schemas.py:15`) to `pydantic.EmailStr | None`, or add a `field_validator` rejecting non-address-shaped strings.
- [ ] Add `max_length` (e.g. 256) to the `/login` password form field (`login.py:129`) and reject oversize input early.
- [ ] Add a unit test for `_safe_next_path` (`login.py:64-67`) asserting it returns the default for `http://evil.com`, `//evil.com`, `\\evil.com`, `""`/`None`, and returns same-origin paths unchanged.

## Why

Verified robustness/accuracy gaps in the LLM client layer. Mostly **latent fragility** today (the learner-facing study-coach route is pinned to the fake provider; only `/authoring-assist/propose` uses the real Anthropic provider), but each is a real defect on the live-provider path:

1. **No provider error handling/retry.** `AnthropicProvider.complete()` calls `client.messages.create(**call_kwargs)` (`src/lms/llm/providers.py:182`) with no try/except, retry, or backoff. Any `anthropic.APIError`/`RateLimitError`/`APITimeoutError` propagates raw (not an `LLMError`); the only real-provider call site `authoring_assist_propose_route` (`api.py:331-359`) catches only `(SourceConstraintViolation, ValueError)`, so a 429/timeout becomes an unhandled 500.
2. **Budget tracker not thread-safe.** LLM routes are sync `def` (FastAPI threadpool); `_default_client()` is `@lru_cache` (`api.py:168`), so all requests share one `DailyBudgetTracker`. `preflight()` reads `self._global_spend` and `record()` does `+=` (`budgets.py:35-36,59`) with no lock — a non-atomic read-modify-write that lets two concurrent calls both pass preflight against a stale spend and overspend the cap.
3. **Preflight under-estimates output cost.** `_estimate_cost` uses `output_tokens = max_tokens if set else max(64, input_tokens)` (`client.py:268`), but when a caller passes `max_tokens=None` the provider sends `default_max_tokens=1024` (`providers.py:147,177`) — so preflight assumes ~64 tokens for a call that can return 1024.
4. **`_estimate_cost` fallback rates wrong scale.** Fallback `input_rate=1_000`, `output_rate=4_000` micro-USD/token (`client.py:269-270`) are ~300× the module's real ~3/15 scale (`providers.py:97-127`); any adapter lacking explicit cost attrs is mis-estimated by ~300×.
5. **Citation enforcement is naive substring.** `SourceConstraintViolation` fires only when `citation not in provider_response.text` (`client.py:148-150`); `flag_uncited_claims` uses the same `source_id not in text` test (`interaction_policy.py:232-237`). A citation id counts as "present" anywhere in the output, trivially satisfiable by echoing the id.
6. **Real-SDK build + error paths untested** (`providers.py:155-157`).

## Scope

Harden `src/lms/llm/{providers,budgets,client}.py`: wrap provider calls in a single `LLMError` subclass with bounded retry, make the budget tracker atomic, align preflight/estimate with real provider behavior, and make citation matching boundary-aware.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT switch the study-coach route off the fake provider, nor change which routes use the real provider.
- Do NOT add a heavyweight retry dependency if a small bounded backoff loop suffices.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: wrapping the provider call without a test proving a `RateLimitError` becomes the wrapper type, or a lock not actually held across read+update, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] Wrap `client.messages.create(...)` in `AnthropicProvider.complete()` (`providers.py:182`) in try/except for the anthropic SDK error types and re-raise as a new `LLMError` subclass (e.g. `ProviderCallError`); add bounded exponential-backoff retry for `RateLimitError`/`APITimeoutError`/5xx.
- [ ] Add a `threading.Lock` to `DailyBudgetTracker` (`budgets.py:25-59`) held across the `preflight()` read and the `record()` update (or a reserve/commit API), so concurrent calls cannot both pass preflight against a stale spend.
- [ ] In `_estimate_cost` (`client.py:260-271`): when `max_tokens is None`, estimate using the provider's `default_max_tokens` (`getattr(provider,"default_max_tokens",1024)`), and change the fallback rates (269-270) to the module micro-USD scale (e.g. `(3, 15)`).
- [ ] Make citation matching boundary-aware in `client.py:145-155` and `interaction_policy.py:232-237` (word-boundary regex or a structured `[[<id>]]` marker requiring co-occurrence with content).
- [ ] Add `tests/llm/` cases: provider `RateLimitError` → `ProviderCallError`; `_estimate_cost(max_tokens=None)` reserves ≈`default_max_tokens`; a fallback-rate adapter estimates on the 3/15 scale; a substring-only citation echo is rejected.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification, capture the FAIL output, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/llm/test_anthropic_provider.py::test_rate_limit_wrapped` passes: a `client_factory` whose `messages.create` raises `RateLimitError` causes `LLMClient.complete()` to raise `ProviderCallError` (an `LLMError`), not the raw SDK error.
- [ ] A test asserts `_estimate_cost` with `max_tokens=None` projects output cost from `default_max_tokens` (≈1024), not 64.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily remove the new try/except in `AnthropicProvider.complete()`. `test_rate_limit_wrapped` **must FAIL** (the raw `RateLimitError` escapes). Restore; it passes. Capture both runs.
- [ ] `pytest tests/llm/ -q` stays green.

## Implementation Notes

- Real-provider call site: `authoring_assist_propose_route` (`api.py:331-359`), today catches only `(SourceConstraintViolation, ValueError)`.
- Module micro-USD price scale: `providers.py:97-127` (validated by `tests/llm/test_anthropic_provider.py:168-180`).
- Confirmed-green today: `pytest tests/llm/ -q` passes.

_Source: 2026-05-30 multi-agent audit (report in PR #190: `docs/audits/2026-05-30-comprehensive-audit.md`)._

## Why

The graph importers have verified robustness gaps on realistic input (all **current breaks**; fail-safe — they abort without corruption, but with a raw traceback instead of a clean `CsvGraphImportError`):

1. **CSV invalid enum / self-prerequisite pass dry-run, then crash mid-import.** `_load_rows` (`src/lms/importers/csv_graph.py:127-175`) validates required columns, duplicate keys, and unknown prerequisite references, but does **not** validate `knowledge_type`/`status`/`ownership_scope`, nor reject a row listing itself as a prerequisite. Those checks happen later in `create_knowledge_node`/`create_knowledge_edge` as generic `ValueError` (not `CsvGraphImportError`). Verified: a row with `knowledge_type=not_a_type` passes `dry_run=True` reporting `nodes=2`, then a real import aborts mid-write — violating the repo's tested "validate-before-writes / dry-run matches real import" invariant (`test_unknown_prerequisite_fails_before_write`).
2. **Setext headings crash the markdown importer.** `_extract_h1_h2_headings` uses Mistune (which recognizes setext headings — a title underlined with `===`/`---`, valid CommonMark), but `_find_heading_line` matches only ATX `#` headings via `_ATX_HEADING_RE` (`markdown.py:17,259`), raising `ValueError("could not map parsed heading to source line")` (`markdown.py:267`). Verified: a file with `Big Title\n=========` aborts `plan_markdown_notes` with a raw traceback.
3. **Non-UTF-8 input crashes both importers.** `import_csv_graph` opens with `encoding="utf-8"` (`csv_graph.py:67`); the markdown importer uses `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (`markdown.py:169`). A latin-1/cp1252 file (common Excel/Windows export) raises an uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError`.

## Scope

Front-load validation and translate decode failures into the importer's own error type so dry-run matches real import and bad input fails cleanly. `src/lms/importers/csv_graph.py` and `src/lms/importers/markdown.py`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the knowledge-graph models or `create_knowledge_node`/`create_knowledge_edge` semantics.
- Do NOT add new CLI subcommands; keep existing CLI behavior (clean error message, non-zero exit).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: validation that still lets an invalid-enum row pass `dry_run` then crash the real import, or a setext file that still raises `ValueError`, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `_load_rows` (`csv_graph.py:127-175`), validate `knowledge_type`/`status`/`ownership_scope` against the graph model enums and reject a row whose prerequisites include its own `_node_key`, raising `CsvGraphImportError` with the row number — so dry-run and real import agree.
- [ ] In `markdown.py`, map heading lines from Mistune token positions, or extend line-finding to recognize setext underlines; at minimum skip-with-logged-warning instead of raising at `markdown.py:267`.
- [ ] Wrap the file reads (`csv_graph.py:67`, `markdown.py:169`) to translate `UnicodeDecodeError` into `CsvGraphImportError` (CSV) / a caught skip-with-warning (markdown), naming the file.
- [ ] Add tests in `tests/importers/`: invalid-enum CSV raises `CsvGraphImportError` under `dry_run=True`; a self-prerequisite row is rejected; a setext-heading markdown file imports without raising; a latin-1 CSV raises `CsvGraphImportError`.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification, capture the FAIL output, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/importers/test_csv_graph_importer.py::test_invalid_enum_rejected_in_dry_run` passes: a CSV row with `knowledge_type=not_a_type` raises `CsvGraphImportError` (not a bare `ValueError`) under `dry_run=True`.

## Why

`FSRS_RULES` is evaluated in order, first match wins (`evidence_to_fsrs_rating`, `src/lms/scheduling/fsrs_adapter.py:188`). The `partial-at-mastery` rule (returns `"good"`, value 3) sits at index 3 (lines 143-150), **before** `supported-or-low-confidence-correct` (returns `"hard"`, value 2) at index 5 (159-166). `_is_score_at_mastery` (111-114) checks only `correctness is not False and score >= 0.85` — it does **not** inspect `hint_used` / `reference_accessed` / `support_level`. So a correct answer that used a revealed hint with `normalized_score=0.95` is rated `"good"`/3, contradicting the explicit intent of the `supported-or-low-confidence-correct` rule ("Correct evidence with support … maps to FSRS Hard"). Reproduced: `support_level="hint", hint_used=True, normalized_score=0.95` → `label="good", value=3, rule_id="partial-at-mastery"`.

This is **latent fragility, not a current learner-facing break**: `_conservative_signal` (`service.py:687-691`) blends FSRS with `_classify_signal` and downgrades supported-correct answers, so the live interval is fine. But the **recorded** FSRS rating (label/value/rule_id in `decision_log` and the `SchedulerDecision` audit row) is over-confident and misleading on the Inspect/explainability surface.

## Scope

Make the partial-credit mastery rules support-aware so a supported correct answer is rated `"hard"` via `supported-or-low-confidence-correct`. `src/lms/scheduling/fsrs_adapter.py` only.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change `_conservative_signal` or live interval selection — only the FSRS rating classification.
- Do NOT reorder unrelated rules or touch the (1,3,7,14,28) ramp.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a change that does not actually move a supported `score>=0.85` answer off `partial-at-mastery`, or a test that does not assert the resulting `rule_id`, is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/lms/scheduling/fsrs_adapter.py`, make `_is_score_at_mastery` (and `_is_score_under_mastery`) support-aware — e.g. add `and not _has_support(record)` — so a supported correct answer falls through `partial-at-mastery` (143-150) to `supported-or-low-confidence-correct` (159-166). (Alternatively, move the support rule ahead of the partial-credit rules in `FSRS_RULES`.)
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/scheduling/test_fsrs_adapter.py` asserting `evidence_to_fsrs_rating` for `correctness=True, support_level="hint", hint_used=True, normalized_score=0.95` returns `label="hard"`, `value=2`, `rule_id="supported-or-low-confidence-correct"`.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture the FAIL output, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/scheduling/test_fsrs_adapter.py::test_supported_high_score_is_hard` passes, asserting `rule_id == "supported-or-low-confidence-correct"` and `value == 2` for the hint-supported `0.95` case.

## Implementation Notes

## Why

`score_work_product()` (`src/lms/cases/repository.py:326-422`) validates rubric presence, case existence, node resolution, and score ranges, but **never checks `work_product.status`**. `WORK_PRODUCT_STATUSES` (`src/lms/cases/models.py:35-42`) includes `scored`, `revision-requested`, `accepted`, and `withdrawn`, so re-running it on a terminal product is structurally possible. Verified by reproduction: scoring the same work product twice produces **2 `EvidenceRecord`s and 2 `RubricScore`s**; `work_product.rubric_score_id` repoints to the second score, leaving the first `RubricScore` + its `EvidenceRecord` orphaned (no FK references them); and `work_product.status` is forced back to `"scored"` (line 421), silently clobbering a `revision-requested`/`accepted` state.

Because each score emits a **transfer `EvidenceRecord`** into the same ledger that `mastery/service.py:41-43` (selects all evidence per node, no dedup) and `mastery/policy.py:29` (`confidence = min(1.0, 0.35 + len(records)*0.12)`) read, duplicate scoring **inflates mastery confidence/evidence_count and capability**. The revision loop (`feedback/repository.py:346` sets `status="revision-requested"`) is a legitimate re-score path that hits this unguarded behavior. This is **latent fragility today** (no HTTP/UI route reaches `score_work_product`; `cases/api.py` exposes only submit/list/get) but a real data-integrity defect once any caller is wired. Tests cover only single scoring (`tests/cases/test_work_products.py:88` asserts exactly 1 evidence record).

## Scope

Add a status guard to `score_work_product` so a work product can only be scored from a scoreable state, and supersede (not orphan) prior score/evidence if a re-score is explicitly allowed. `src/lms/cases/repository.py` only.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT expose a new scoring HTTP route or change `cases/api.py` surface.
- Do NOT change the mastery/capability estimators — fixing the duplicate-source at the write path is the correct layer.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a guard that does not actually block a second `score_work_product` call on a `scored` product, or leaving the prior `RubricScore`/`EvidenceRecord` orphaned on an allowed re-score, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] At the top of `score_work_product` (`src/lms/cases/repository.py:326`), guard the transition: raise `ValueError("work product is not in a scoreable state")` unless `work_product.status in ("submitted", "draft")` (plus an explicit `revision-requested` re-score path if supported).
- [ ] If a `revision-requested` re-score is allowed, supersede the prior score: delete or mark `superseded` the `RubricScore` + `EvidenceRecord` referenced by `work_product.rubric_score_id` before creating the new ones, matching the supersession pattern at `src/lms/feedback/repository.py:328`.
- [ ] Add tests in `tests/cases/test_work_products.py`: (a) re-scoring a `scored` product raises `ValueError`; (b) after an allowed `revision-requested` re-score there is exactly **one** non-superseded `RubricScore` and **one** transfer `EvidenceRecord` for the (learner, node).
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture the FAIL output, then revert.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/cases/test_work_products.py::test_rescore_terminal_product_rejected` passes: a second `score_work_product` on a product already in `"scored"` raises `ValueError` and creates **no** additional `EvidenceRecord` (query count stays 1).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily delete the new status-guard line. The test above **must FAIL** (the second score succeeds and a 2nd `EvidenceRecord`/`RubricScore` appears). Restore the guard; the test passes. Capture both runs.
- [ ] `pytest tests/cases/ tests/mastery/ -q` stays green.

## Implementation Notes

- Re-score reproduction (confirmed): call `score_work_product` twice on one product → 2 `EvidenceRecord`s, 2 `RubricScore`s, `rubric_score_id` on the second, status forced to `scored`.
- Supersession precedent to mirror: `src/lms/feedback/repository.py:328` (`prior.status = "superseded"`).
- Confirmed-green today: `pytest tests/cases/test_work_products.py -q` passes (single-score path only).

_Source: 2026-05-30 multi-agent audit (report in PR #190: `docs/audits/2026-05-30-comprehensive-audit.md`)._

## Why

The README "Spacing improves retention" commitment is implemented but **never runs in production**. Two verified, current breaks:

1. **Engine not wired.** `schedule_from_attempt()` and `seed_new_learning_item()` (`src/lms/scheduling/service.py:649-816`) are referenced **only** from `tests/scheduling/*` — no `src/` module calls them. The two production modules that import scheduling, `src/lms/ui/attempts.py:55-92` and `src/lms/evidence/api.py:23-33`, never schedule a review, so recording an attempt never creates or advances a `ReviewQueueItem`.
2. **Success ramp frozen at step 0.** The interval comes from `_success_interval_days(prior_successes)` over `SUCCESS_INTERVALS_DAYS = (1, 3, 7, 14, 28)`. `prior_successes` is `_count_prior_successful_reviews`, which counts `ReviewQueueItem.status == "completed"` (`service.py:257`). **No production code path ever sets a queue item to `"completed"`** (repo-wide search: the only `"completed"` write is for `FeedbackAction` at `feedback/repository.py:404`). Reproduced: four consecutive successful reviews of one node all emit `rule="success-ramp-step-0"` with `prior_successes=0` → every success reschedules at 1 day forever. The only advancement test (`tests/scheduling/test_review_queue.py:186`) manually sets `first.status = "completed"` at line 195, masking the gap.

This is a **current break** (a load-bearing product promise unfulfilled at runtime), not latent fragility.

## Scope

Wire the existing scheduler into the attempt/evidence write path and give `_count_prior_successful_reviews` a real data source, so a learner's successful reviews actually expand 1 → 3 → 7 → 14 → 28 days. Engine internals (interval math, FSRS mapping) are already built and stay as-is.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT rewrite the interval ramp, FSRS adapter, or remediation/pause/resume logic — they are correct and tested; this issue only connects them to the runtime.
- Do NOT change learner-facing attempt markup beyond the minimum needed to invoke scheduling.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: adding a `schedule_from_attempt` call that the real attempt path never reaches, or a test that manually sets `status="completed"` instead of exercising the production completion transition, is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break gate below must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In the path that already creates an `EvidenceRecord` — `src/lms/feedback/scoring.py` `score_attempt_with_rubric` (and/or `src/lms/evidence/api.py:23-33`) — call `schedule_from_attempt(...)` (`src/lms/scheduling/service.py:649`) after the evidence is created, passing learner/node/signal so a `ReviewQueueItem` is created or advanced.
- [ ] Add a review-completion transition production actually writes: a repository helper in `src/lms/scheduling/` plus a `POST /review-queue/{id}/complete` route in `src/lms/scheduling/api.py` (today it exposes only GET) that sets `ReviewQueueItem.status = "completed"`, invoked when a due review is satisfied — so `_count_prior_successful_reviews` (`service.py:247-261`) reads real data.
- [ ] Add an end-to-end test `tests/scheduling/test_runtime_wiring.py` that records 3 successful attempts for one (learner, node) through the **production** path (no manual `status` edits) and asserts the scheduled `due_at` gap advances 1 → 3 → 7 days.
- [ ] Perform the deliberate-break verification (see Acceptance Criteria), capture the FAIL output, then revert the break.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Named test `tests/scheduling/test_runtime_wiring.py` passes: after 3 production-path successful reviews of one node, the emitted rule is `success-ramp-step-2` (equivalently, consecutive `due_at` deltas are 1, 3, 7 days), proving the ramp advances with **no** manual `status="completed"` edit.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate:** temporarily comment out the new `schedule_from_attempt(...)` call in `feedback/scoring.py`. With it removed, `tests/scheduling/test_runtime_wiring.py` **must FAIL** (no `ReviewQueueItem` is created/advanced for the learner). Restore the call; the test passes. Capture both runs in the PR.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scheduling/ -q` stays green (existing scheduler tests do not regress).

## Implementation Notes

- Scheduler API: `schedule_from_attempt` / `seed_new_learning_item` at `src/lms/scheduling/service.py:649-816`; ramp at `service.py:247-261` (`SUCCESS_INTERVALS_DAYS`, `_success_interval_days`, `_count_prior_successful_reviews`).
- Confirmed-green today: `pytest tests/scheduling/ -q` passes — the engine works in isolation; it is simply never called from `src/`.
- Recommended seam: invoke scheduling immediately after `create_evidence_record(...)` so every recorded retrieval feeds the queue.

**Why**
`README.md:175` tells readers the `src/lms/` modules "(`api`, `auth`, `curriculum`, `evidence`, `feedback`, `graphs`, `llm`, `mastery`, `scheduling`, `analytics`) are intentionally empty placeholders." That is materially false today -- those modules carry full SQLAlchemy models, repositories, services, and ~20 FastAPI routers, with 33 Alembic migrations and a passing test suite. A new contributor or reviewer reading the README would badly mis-assess the project's maturity. Separately, a leftover bootstrap template package `src/my_project/` survives with `greet`/`add` stubs (`src/my_project/main.py:4-13`); it is still imported by the placeholder tests (`tests/test_main.py:5`, `tests/__init__.py:1`) and wired into coverage/lint config (`pyproject.toml:73,77,112`), so it inflates the module list and clutters tooling.

**Scope**
Update the "Running The Backend Locally" section so it describes the real module set and current capabilities, and fully remove the `my_project` template package along with the test files and config references that depend on it. Removal must be complete (package + tests + `pyproject.toml` coverage/lint entries), not partial.

**Non-Goals**
- Rewriting the product vision, milestone list, or `docs/product/project-plan.md`.
- Touching any `src/lms/` functional code.
- Deleting `src/my_project/` while leaving `tests/test_main.py` importing it (would break collection) -- a partial removal does NOT satisfy this issue.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Replace the "intentionally empty placeholders" paragraph (`README.md:173-175`) with an accurate summary of the implemented module set and capabilities, and add a one-line note that the LLM study-coach layer currently runs on `FakeProvider` until a real Anthropic adapter lands (cross-reference the provider issue).
- [ ] Delete `src/my_project/` (package + `__init__.py`/`main.py`) and `src/my_project.egg-info/`.
- [ ] Delete the placeholder tests that import it -- `tests/test_main.py` (`:5`) -- and remove the `my_project` reference in `tests/__init__.py` (`:1`).
- [ ] Remove `my_project` from `pyproject.toml`: the `--cov=my_project` in `addopts` (`:73`), the `source = ["lms", "my_project"]` coverage entry (`:77`), and the `known-first-party` list (`:112`).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] `grep -rn "my_project" src tests pyproject.toml` returns no matches after the change (currently it matches `src/my_project/__init__.py:3`, `tests/test_main.py:5`, `tests/__init__.py:1`, and `pyproject.toml:73,77,112`).
- [ ] The README no longer contains the string "intentionally empty placeholders" and accurately lists the implemented modules.
- [ ] `uv run pytest` collects and passes with no errors from the removed module, and `make check` passes (smoke gate: confirms the coverage/lint config no longer references the deleted package).

**Implementation Notes**

body:
**Why**
Content-hash drift detection is a named Milestone-2 v1 capability (`README.md:215`) and the `SourceReference` schema enumerates `markdown-file`, `kindle-highlight`, `url`, `pdf-passage`, and `internal-note` types. But `scan_source_references` silently buckets every non-markdown reference into `skipped` and continues: `if reference.source_type != "markdown-file": skipped += 1; continue` (`src/lms/sources/repository.py:215-217`). Consequently a stale URL or a changed internal note can never surface as `drift_status == "stale"`, so "this prompt may be built on stale source material" is undetectable for the majority of documented source types. The skip is also indistinguishable, in `DriftScanSummary` (`src/lms/sources/repository.py:22-30`), from "deliberately unsupported," so an operator cannot tell coverage gaps from no-ops.

**Scope**
Add drift handling for `internal-note` (hash the stored content) and `url` (fetch + hash, behind a network-off-by-default flag so CI stays hermetic), and make `DriftScanSummary` report per-type *reasons* for non-scanned references (e.g. `unsupported_pdf`, `unsupported_kindle`) instead of one opaque `skipped` count. **Privacy note:** the URL-fetch path is a deterministic program fetching public source URLs (no LLM, no proprietary-data egress to SaaS), which is permitted; keep it opt-in and never send note *content* outward -- it only GETs the cited source.

**Non-Goals**
- Kindle annotation-DB integration and PDF text extraction stay deferred -- but they MUST be reported as explicitly `unsupported_*` rather than silently skipped.
- Sending any proprietary note text to an external service.
- A change that adds branches but leaves `internal-note`/`url` still falling through to the skip path does NOT satisfy this issue.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Branch `scan_source_references` (`src/lms/sources/repository.py:205-258`) on `reference.source_type`: keep the `markdown-file` path, add an `internal-note` path that hashes stored content, and add a `url` path that fetches + hashes only when an `allow_network` flag (default `False`) is passed.
- [ ] Extend `compute_source_hash_for_reference` (`src/lms/sources/repository.py:183-202`) so `internal-note` hashes stored content and (when network is allowed) `url` hashes fetched bytes, instead of raising `ValueError` for all non-file types (current behavior at `:202`).
- [ ] Replace the single `skipped` field on `DriftScanSummary` (`src/lms/sources/repository.py:22-30`) with explicit per-reason counts (e.g. `skipped`, `unsupported_pdf`, `unsupported_kindle`) or an attached reason map, and populate it in the scan loop.
- [ ] Update the `lms source scan` CLI rendering (the scan subcommand at `src/lms/__main__.py:48-58`) to print the new per-reason breakdown.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] New test cases in `tests/sources/test_drift_scan.py` (which currently only covers markdown) that fail on `main` and pass after: (1) an `internal-note` whose stored content changed flips `drift_status` to `stale`; (2) a `url` reference flips to `stale` when its fetched content changes, using a mocked/injected fetcher with `allow_network=True` (no live network).
- [ ] A test asserts a `pdf-passage` and a `kindle-highlight` reference are counted under explicit `unsupported_*` reasons in `DriftScanSummary`, distinct from `skipped`/`scanned`.
- [ ] A test asserts that with the default `allow_network=False`, `url` references are not fetched and the scan issues no network call.
- [ ] `make check` passes and the default `pytest` run performs no live network I/O.

**Implementation Notes**
The hashing helpers and audit-event recording already exist (`compute_source_hash` at `src/lms/sources/repository.py:33-52`; audit write at `:242-251`). For the `url` fetcher, inject a callable (default a thin `requests`/`urllib` wrapper) so tests pass a fake -- mirror the hermetic, opt-in network posture used for the Playwright harness (`PLAYWRIGHT_AVAILABLE` gating, `docs/development/web-prototype.md:80-96`). Preserve the existing `current`/`stale`/`missing` transition and the `if reference.drift_status == new_status: continue` short-circuit (`:238-239`) so audit events only fire on real status changes.
